results: 1. nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
2. whole exome sequencing: heterozygous likely pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) - CMT1H
3. MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
4. MRI spine: symmetrical thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H) due to heterozygous FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) mutation, with hypertrophic neuropathy involving cranial nerves and cauda equina.

Alternatives to consider:
1. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) — but the definitive pathogenic FBLN5 variant makes this far less likely.
2. Hereditary demyelinating neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies (HNPP) from PMP22 deletion — typically has a different phenotype and is not associated with FBLN5.
3. A different FBLN5-associated connective tissue/neurologic overlap (e.g., cutis laxa/age-related macular degeneration spectrum) coincident with an acquired demyelinating neuropathy — unlikely given the integrated genetic and imaging findings.
dx: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H) due to heterozygous FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) mutation, with hypertrophic neuropathy involving cranial nerves and cauda equina.
